command.reason: Locate the frame grasp block, frame ends, stand opening and tool from calibrated visible surface points.
Grasp the frame at its black block and lift it clear of the table to inspect the captured frame and insertion shaft.
The frame remained on the table and the fingers closed fully, so lower the open gripper to the frame with enough settling time before closing.
Close on the centered frame block, then raise it fully to verify the grasp and expose its geometry.
Measure the lifted shaft direction and tip and the stand opening to compute a downward insertion orientation.
Rotate the measured long frame shaft downward and carry its tip just above the stand opening while maintaining the grasp.
Check shaft tilt and tip offset relative to the stand before inserting; the camera shows lateral misalignment.
Correct the measured shaft tilt to vertical and center it over the stand, lowering the tip close to the opening.
Insert the vertically aligned long shaft into the stand with a straight downward motion.
Seat the frame farther into the stand, release the block, and withdraw to inspect whether the assembly remains upright.
The frame moved with the open gripper rather than remaining in the stand; remeasure its exposed shaft to recover the placement.
Reclose to secure the displaced frame and move the currently observed shaft tip over the stand for a corrected insertion.
Measure the shaft after regrasping so its actual axis, rather than its earlier slipped pose, determines the insertion alignment.
Straighten the current shaft axis, align it to the stand center and insert it while holding the regrasped frame.
The downward motion stopped at the stand rim; measure the visible shaft and opening for a small lateral correction.
Lift off the rim, shift the shaft about five millimetres toward the opening center, and retry the vertical insertion.
The shaft has entered the stand. Release it and withdraw backward along the gripper approach axis so the palm clears the frame without carrying it away.
The released frame remains upright in the stand. Approach the tool handle from above with the finger closing direction across its width, then grasp it.
Lift the tool clear of the table and inspect the larger hole and the now settled hook before aligning them.
Locate the larger tool-hole center from its rim and the hook tip and horizontal bar to plan threading.
Rotate the tool upright with its larger hole above the handle, then align that hole just outside the hook tip.
Check the actual hole center after rotation against the hook tip before threading it; grasp settling can shift the tool.
Center the larger hole laterally on the hook and slide it over the raised tip onto the horizontal bar.
The hook bar is visible through the larger hole. Lower the tool onto it, release, and retreat away from the hanging tool to check that it remains supported.
The tool fell after release, so the hole was not securely threaded. Locate its new handle and hole positions for one recovery attempt.
Regrasp the fallen tool handle for a final placement attempt.
Lift the recovered tool horizontally and bring its larger hole above the hook's upward tip for a direct downward threading attempt.
The upward hook tip now passes through the larger hole. Release the tool and move the open gripper away so gravity can seat it on the hook.

scope: Offline measurements, not automatic causal attribution. Raw wrist loads include gravity and dynamics.

wall_time_components.note: Dispatch-to-delivered-response includes message delivery delay. Native completed-turn duration is separately exported in policy_usage. Simulated control time is separate; residual is not model latency.
